Rabbi Daniel Walker said rising antisemitism, combined with a lack of action to "deal with core problems", had left many members of Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation in Manchester – and British Jews more widely – feeling increasingly vulnerable as the anniversary of the attack approaches. "I think we're actually almost in a harder position than we were even immediately after the attack," he said ahead of a memorial service for the victims and survivors which will take place later today. "I think the sense of vulnerability has grown. It hasn't diminished." evidence_packet.evidence_text: Teen who went into care at 10 calls system 'fundamentally flawed' - BBC News Image caption, Hayden said he would like to see significant changes in the care system By Lauren Hirst North West Published 30 August 2026 A teenager who went into care when he was 10 has described how he struggled to navigate the system and seek help. Hayden, now aged 17, lived in a children's home until he was 16 before moving into a semi-independent home. After feeling unsafe there he ended up sofa-surfing. "There is an incredible amount of individuals working so hard to improve the lives of young people but the system is fundamentally flawed," said Hayden, who got in touch with the BBC via Your Voice to share his experience. A new government-commissioned report found that young adult care-leavers have a death rate about four times higher than the general population . The report noted the potentially catastrophic consequences for those who are often left alone "with no safety net". People leaving care in England at 18 often lose "significant levers of support", the report concluded, as it warned the so-called "care cliff" must be addressed. "You kind of are navigating it by yourself and just hoping you've said the right things and put the right things forward to make things happen," said Hayden, who grew up in Middleton, Greater Manchester, before being placed in care in a different local authority area. "We are not the undeserving poor of the Victorian era. "People deserve compassion because they have been through so much." evidence_packet.evidence_text: The street outside legendary indie club 42s, a front garden on Burnage Lane and a pub's function room with a tiny stage - all locations in Manchester where you could have found Courteeners in their early days The four school friends from Middleton, near Rochdale, have certainly come a long way since they hit the Manchester indie scene in 2006 While they have travelled around the world ever since, there is no place like home and they will take to the stage later for a huge homecoming gig at Wythenshawe Park From humble beginnings performing for friends in the garden of their shared house in Burnage, the Courteeners are now celebrating 20 years together Fresh from releasing a new best-of compilation album called God Bless The Band, lead singer and songwriter Liam Fray spoke to BBC North West Tonight at The Briton's Protection pub on Deansgate, where he first performed as a solo artist back in 2005 Sitting upstairs in the pub, Fray smiled at the 3ft (0.9m) stage and single spotlight on the ceiling while recalling the night he spent there more than two decades ago

title: The Stockport shed cleaner who was awarded Victoria Cross

evidence_packet.title: The Stockport shed cleaner who was awarded Victoria Cross
evidence_packet.lead: Wilfred Wood was working on the railways as a shed cleaner when World War One broke out in 1914
evidence_packet.summary: Wilfred Wood was working on the railways as a shed cleaner when World War One broke out in 1914
evidence_packet.evidence_text: When World War One broke out in 1914, Wilfred Wood was working on the railways as a shed cleaner But by the end of 1916, he had enlisted in the Cheshire Regiment of the British Army where he trained as a stretcher bearer to collect the wounded from the battlefields He was then transferred to the 10th Battalion Northumberland Fusiliers where he would later take part in one of the last battles of the World War One involving British soldiers fighting in Italy The Battle of Vittorio Veneto was fought from 24 October to 3 November 1918 and was seen as a decisive victory that contributed to the end of the war Mark Smith, who is a medals specialist at Stanley Gibbons Baldwins, said Wood went above and beyond what was expected of him and used his own initiative when his unit was held up by hostile machine guns and snipers The Stockport shed cleaner given the Victoria Cross

evidence_packet.summary: When World War One broke out in 1914, Wilfred Wood was working on the railways as a shed cleaner But by the end of 1916, he had enlisted in the Cheshire Regiment of the British Army where he trained as a stretcher bearer to collect the wounded from the battlefields He was then tr
evidence_packet.evidence_text: When World War One broke out in 1914, Wilfred Wood was working on the railways as a shed cleaner But by the end of 1916, he had enlisted in the Cheshire Regiment of the British Army where he trained as a stretcher bearer to collect the wounded from the battlefields He was then transferred to the 10th Battalion Northumberland Fusiliers where he would later take part in one of the last battles of the World War One involving British soldiers fighting in Italy The Battle of Vittorio Veneto was fought from 24 October to 3 November 1918 and was seen as a decisive victory that contributed to the end of the war Mark Smith, who is a medals specialist at Stanley Gibbons Baldwins, said Wood went above and beyond what was expected of him and used his own initiative when his unit was held up by hostile machine guns and snipers The Stockport shed cleaner given the Victoria Cross

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Heywood Bosses issue update after Andy Burnham promise on Heywood getting Metrolink Last year Andy Burnham said spades will be in the ground on the project in Heywood by 2028 Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 07:51, 31 Aug 2026 Vie Metrolink trams to Heywood have been promised by Andy Burnham. Last year, the former Greater Manchester mayor even said spades could be in the ground by 2028 Now Mr Burnham sits in Downing Street as Prime Minister, his successor in the city-region, Bev Craig, hasn’t mentioned the project. She did speak about the expansion of the tram network to Stockport in her manifesto, but Heywood was omitted Despite this, Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has confirmed they are working on a business case for the Heywood project. It falls under what TfGM calls the Oldham-Rochdale-Heywood-Bury Tram-Train pathfinder The new Metrolink line would connect Bury to Rochdale via Heywood and then loop back through Shaw towards Oldham . However, no plans have been formally approved When opened, the scheme would give Greater Manchester two Metrolink firsts: The first ‘orbital’ Metrolink route, i.e. one which does not go via the city centre, and the first ‘tram-train’, set to be rolled out across the city in coming years

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale Police flood Rochdale town centre to 'restore peace' after boy, 13, stabbed in Taco Bell toilets Gangs of roaming yobs in face coverings armed with weapons have been reported Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 14:35, 30 Aug 2026 Updated 16:3 A boy aged 13 was stabbed in a toilet of a town centre's Taco Bell restaurant in a 'serious and sustained attack' which could have had 'far more tragic consequences', police chiefs have said Rochdale town centre and a defined area around it, meanwhile, will be flooded with officers from Sunday afternoon to 'restore peace' after multiple reports of gangs of roaming yobs in face coverings armed with weapons, Greater Manchester Police added The teenage boy was knifed inside the restaurant on Riverside Walk in the town centre after claims dozens of youths , some carrying knives, ran inside. In an update on Sunday, GMP said he remained in hospital for treatment with serious injuries Two teenage boys were later arrested on suspicion of assault and possession of a bladed article. They remained in custody for questioning on Sunday, GMP added in the update, with 'enquiries to identify others involved' currently ongoing Police chiefs also pointed to 'wider disorder' occurring, although details of any other incidents haven't been disclosed. In response, enhanced stop-and-search powers have been authorised for officers on the ground to use, enabling them to order youths to remove all face covering

evidence_packet.lead: Heywood Bosses issue update after Andy Burnham promise on Heywood getting Metrolink Last year Andy Burnham said spades will be in the ground on the project in Heywood by 2028 Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 07:51, 31 Aug 2026 Vie Metrolink trams to Heywood h
evidence_packet.summary: Heywood Bosses issue update after Andy Burnham promise on Heywood getting Metrolink Last year Andy Burnham said spades will be in the ground on the project in Heywood by 2028 Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 07:51, 31 Aug 2026 Vie Metrolink trams to Heywood h
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Heywood Bosses issue update after Andy Burnham promise on Heywood getting Metrolink Last year Andy Burnham said spades will be in the ground on the project in Heywood by 2028 Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 07:51, 31 Aug 2026 Vie Metrolink trams to Heywood have been promised by Andy Burnham. Last year, the former Greater Manchester mayor even said spades could be in the ground by 2028 Now Mr Burnham sits in Downing Street as Prime Minister, his successor in the city-region, Bev Craig, hasn’t mentioned the project. She did speak about the expansion of the tram network to Stockport in her manifesto, but Heywood was omitted Despite this, Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has confirmed they are working on a business case for the Heywood project. It falls under what TfGM calls the Oldham-Rochdale-Heywood-Bury Tram-Train pathfinder The new Metrolink line would connect Bury to Rochdale via Heywood and then loop back through Shaw towards Oldham . However, no plans have been formally approved When opened, the scheme would give Greater Manchester two Metrolink firsts: The first ‘orbital’ Metrolink route, i.e. one which does not go via the city centre, and the first ‘tram-train’, set to be rolled out across the city in coming years

evidence_packet.lead: Manchester canal lost for 91 years after gigantic breach is set to resurface within months A new cafe and canoe and kayak school will be features of the restored length of waterway Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 07:11, 31 Aug 2026 Vi A section of canal lost sinc
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester canal lost for 91 years after gigantic breach is set to resurface within months A new cafe and canoe and kayak school will be features of the restored length of waterway Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 07:11, 31 Aug 2026 Vi A section of canal lost sinc
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester canal lost for 91 years after gigantic breach is set to resurface within months A new cafe and canoe and kayak school will be features of the restored length of waterway Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 07:11, 31 Aug 2026 Vi A section of canal lost since it collapsed 90 years ago is set to be ‘in water’ and enjoyed by the public within months. Part of the Manchester, Bolton and Bury canal near Little Lever was breached in July 1936 Millions of gallons of water from the channel came cascading down into the River Irwell below. The gigantic breach happened close to the Nob End locks, on the canal’s arm towards Bury, with the affected section never restored But work done by Watson Homes, who are building a new 255 home estate alongside the affected waterway at the former Creams Mill site in Little Lever, is set to change that Watson has been restoring a 800 metre section of the waterway as part of the planning permission. The extensive work means the section of canal is set to be ‘in water’ by May 2027 The new section of waterway will also create a destination for visitors as a new café is planned alongside a canoe and kayaking school

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cheshire Police Police officer who has shown 'no remorse over his actions' loses career William Matthews would have been sacked if he had not already resigned Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 06:41, 31 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Cheshire Constabulary ( A police officer sent and received messages on his mobile phone which 'indicated familiarity and association to controlled drug use and recreational use of Nitrous Oxide gas' Former police constable William Matthews would have been sacked had he not already resigned. A judgement arising from a misconduct hearing has now been published Former PC Matthews was working within a force's firearms department at the time. He was also said to have 'undertook online activity which indicated familiarity and association to controlled drug use and recreational use of Nitrous Oxide gas' The hearing at Cheshire Constabulary found the allegations to be proven. He resigned on August 3, ahead of the hearing Chief Constable Mark Roberts ruled former PC Matthews’ conduct was 'undoubtedly gross misconduct'

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Everyone's talking about Stockport and people are moving from Manchester - this is why Stockport has more focus on it now than ever before with Andy Burnham as Prime Minister. But what does that mean for the town once dubbed a 's***hole'? Vi Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 06:08, 31 Aug 2026 Updated 06:38, 31 Aug 2026 "10 years ago people wouldn't have come to Stockport. You would have come if you were looking to go to Boots but it wasn't a destination place." Emma Bedford has just opened her shop Mooch with husband Mark. It's one of Stockport's newest businesses, on the historic Underbanks A network of cobbled streets in and around the town's historic market, the streets are lined with a range of different cafes, the odd bakery, bars, and shops Just 13 years ago, Stockport had the highest rate of empty shops out of any in the UK with things were on a downward spiral and one person telling the Manchester Evening News it was a 's***hole' While it is still tough for independents, things are very different with new businesses opening all the time and people describing it is the next Northern Quarter

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Royal Manchester Children's Hospital Royal Manchester Children's Hospital's special message to Red Arrows after spectacular display "Not only did you brighten up our grey Manchester sky, you certainly brightened up the day for many of our children" Co The world-famous aerobatics display team of the RAF will be taking part in the Southport Airshow this weekend. On the return journey to RAF Warrington on Sunday, the team will fly directly over Greater Manchester, with a special flypast over the hospital The route saw the team fly over Lymm, onto Altrincham and then directly over the city centre, before heading out into Tameside and Oldham . From there, the team flew back to their base at RAF Waddington, in Lincolnshire Earlier this week, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust announced that the Red Arrows would be doing the flypast to 'support them and create a memorable moment' for the children receiving care at the Children's Hospital In a post, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust said: "We're excited to share that this bank holiday weekend we're in for a real treat - and we want you to enjoy it with us "The world-famous RAF Red Arrows will be carrying out a flypast over Royal Manchester Children's Hospital this Sunday at around 5.15pm - subject to weather and other operational factors on the day

evidence_packet.summary: Stockport Fears plans to tackle A555 flooding in Stockport could have disastrous impact The road has been repeatedly hit by flooding. Those living nearby fear plans to tackle that could make things worse
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Fears plans to tackle A555 flooding in Stockport could have disastrous impact The road has been repeatedly hit by flooding. Those living nearby fear plans to tackle that could make things worse. News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 17 People living near the A555 fear a plan to stop the road flooding could be a 'recipe for disaster' Less than 10 years old, the A555 has faced ‘longstanding challenges’, causing major disruption for drivers. The road links Stockport and Manchester Airport to the wider network but after it opened in 2018, it has been repeatedly affected by flooding Work was done to try and solve the problem but the road has still continued to flood. On New Year’s Eve and New Year's Day between 2024 and 2025, the road had to be completely closed to traffic Stockport council looked at what further measures could be taken with interventions to improve drainage around Woodford with work completed in July this year. Drainage from the Highfield Parkway housing estate and Woodford’s Recreation Ground will now be diverted into Spath Brook View 6 Images Flooding on the A555 in 2025 (Image: Jason Roberts /Manchester Evening News)

evidence_packet.summary: NHS Northern Care Alliance in crisis: Failings, strikes and a backlog of complaints as NHS trust faces serious questions Fresh concerns over patient care at Northern Care Alliance, including a backlog of complaints and lengthy waits, have been laid ba News Bethan Finighan Science
evidence_packet.evidence_text: NHS Northern Care Alliance in crisis: Failings, strikes and a backlog of complaints as NHS trust faces serious questions Fresh concerns over patient care at Northern Care Alliance, including a backlog of complaints and lengthy waits, have been laid ba News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 16:59, 30 Aug 2026 The Northern Care Alliance (NCA) has been warned that urgent action is needed to address patient care concerns - with the NHS trust facing a backlog of hundreds of complaints, according to newly published board The trust's own reports, published on Friday (August 28), show the NCA remains under pressure following a series of inspections and patient safety concerns The trust - which runs Salford Royal, Royal Oldham Hospital, Fairfield General Hospital and Rochdale Infirmary - has faced criticism after its own board papers revealed dozens of patients died or 'came to harm ' due to treatment delays and serious errors made by staff working und A total of 28 deaths were found to be linked to lengthy delays last year, with 56 issues of 'severe harm' and 10 deaths linked to problems diagnosing illness recorded The NCA has also faced disruption caused by strike action. evidence_packet.title: ‘We lost our precious baby but became parents to three more beautiful children'
evidence_packet.lead: Real Life ‘We lost our precious baby but became parents to three more beautiful children’ Tragedy was a 'signpost' to a new life for Sarah Hopes and her husband Tom Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 16:05, 30 Aug 2026 View 4 Images Sarah Hope Sarah Hopes and her husband
evidence_packet.summary: Real Life ‘We lost our precious baby but became parents to three more beautiful children’ Tragedy was a 'signpost' to a new life for Sarah Hopes and her husband Tom Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 16:05, 30 Aug 2026 View 4 Images Sarah Hope Sarah Hopes and her husband
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Real Life ‘We lost our precious baby but became parents to three more beautiful children’ Tragedy was a 'signpost' to a new life for Sarah Hopes and her husband Tom Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 16:05, 30 Aug 2026 View 4 Images Sarah Hope Sarah Hopes and her husband Tom had always wanted their children close together in age. So when they found out they were pregnant again, when their daughter was just one, they were overjoyed However, just 12 weeks into the pregnancy, they received devastating news. Vet Sarah, 42, and IT manager Tom, 44, were informed that the baby had a serious fetal developmental abnormality known as Anencephaly, which affects the growth of the brain, skull, and scalp Medical staff told them the condition was 'incompatible with life' and recommended that they terminate the pregnancy Sarah said they had to have a ‘real conversation’ about what to do, but said: “We knew that our baby already had life and purpose inside the womb; he was ours and so wanted “There was a possibility he could live through a full-term pregnancy, and that we would meet him alive once born; we hoped and prayed this would be.”

In an update on Sunday, GMP said he remained in hospital for treatment with serious injuries Two teenage boys were later arrested on suspicion of assault and possession of a bladed article. They remained in custody for questioning on Sunday, GMP added in the update, with 'enquiries to identify others involved' currently ongoing Police chiefs also pointed to 'wider disorder' occurring, although details of any other incidents haven't been disclosed. In response, enhanced stop-and-search powers have been authorised for officers on the ground to use, enabling them to order youths to remove all face covering

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Train drivers including those operating on the London to Manchester line used by Andy Burnham are set to receive an above-inflation pay rise of 3.6 per cent, it's been revealed The wage deal between Avanti West Coast and the Aslef union is the first to be approved under the Prime Minister, who frequently travels up from the capital to work at No 10 North The company runs services from London to destinations including Glasgow, Manchester, Liverpool and Blackpool Aslef has secured time-and-a-half pay on Sundays, a single-year wage rise of 3.6 per cent – 0.7 per cent higher than the latest inflation rate – and up to £720 for turning up to work on a fifth day of the working week, as first reported by the Sunday Times It comes after the union announced plans at the end of June to ballot members in the following weeks on whether to launch strikes in a dispute over pay An Aslef spokesperson said on Saturday: “Our job is to enhance our members’ terms and conditions and this deal, struck with Avanti West Coast and approved by the DFTO (Department for Transport Operator), has been accepted."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford 'In the house Julius was killed, he got to his knees and begged for forgiveness' In December 2023, the body of Tanyaradzwa Julius Matera was found in undergrowth in Higher Broughton - now a coroner has demanded a new investigation into his mur News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 15:52, 30 Aug 2026 Nearly two months after her friend Tanyaradzwa Julius Matera disappeared, Dorothy Wood attended a gathering at 99 Greater Cheetham Street West, Salford What she heard there would prompt a police search. title: Bosses issue update after Andy Burnham promise on Heywood getting Metrolink

evidence_packet.title: Bosses issue update after Andy Burnham promise on Heywood getting Metrolink
evidence_packet.lead: Heywood Bosses issue update after Andy Burnham promise on Heywood getting Metrolink Last year Andy Burnham said spades will be in the ground on the project in Heywood by 2028 Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 07:51, 31 Aug 2026 Vie Metrolink trams to Heywood h
evidence_packet.summary: Heywood Bosses issue update after Andy Burnham promise on Heywood getting Metrolink Last year Andy Burnham said spades will be in the ground on the project in Heywood by 2028 Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 07:51, 31 Aug 2026 Vie Metrolink trams to Heywood h
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Heywood Bosses issue update after Andy Burnham promise on Heywood getting Metrolink Last year Andy Burnham said spades will be in the ground on the project in Heywood by 2028 Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 07:51, 31 Aug 2026 Vie Metrolink trams to Heywood have been promised by Andy Burnham. Last year, the former Greater Manchester mayor even said spades could be in the ground by 2028 Now Mr Burnham sits in Downing Street as Prime Minister, his successor in the city-region, Bev Craig, hasn’t mentioned the project. She did speak about the expansion of the tram network to Stockport in her manifesto, but Heywood was omitted Despite this, Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has confirmed they are working on a business case for the Heywood project. It falls under what TfGM calls the Oldham-Rochdale-Heywood-Bury Tram-Train pathfinder The new Metrolink line would connect Bury to Rochdale via Heywood and then loop back through Shaw towards Oldham . However, no plans have been formally approved When opened, the scheme would give Greater Manchester two Metrolink firsts: The first ‘orbital’ Metrolink route, i.e. one which does not go via the city centre, and the first ‘tram-train’, set to be rolled out across the city in coming years

title: Manchester canal lost for 91 years after gigantic breach is set to resurface within months

evidence_packet.title: Manchester canal lost for 91 years after gigantic breach is set to resurface within months
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester canal lost for 91 years after gigantic breach is set to resurface within months A new cafe and canoe and kayak school will be features of the restored length of waterway Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 07:11, 31 Aug 2026 Vi A section of canal lost sinc
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester canal lost for 91 years after gigantic breach is set to resurface within months A new cafe and canoe and kayak school will be features of the restored length of waterway Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 07:11, 31 Aug 2026 Vi A section of canal lost sinc
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester canal lost for 91 years after gigantic breach is set to resurface within months A new cafe and canoe and kayak school will be features of the restored length of waterway Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 07:11, 31 Aug 2026 Vi A section of canal lost since it collapsed 90 years ago is set to be ‘in water’ and enjoyed by the public within months. Part of the Manchester, Bolton and Bury canal near Little Lever was breached in July 1936 Millions of gallons of water from the channel came cascading down into the River Irwell below. The gigantic breach happened close to the Nob End locks, on the canal’s arm towards Bury, with the affected section never restored But work done by Watson Homes, who are building a new 255 home estate alongside the affected waterway at the former Creams Mill site in Little Lever, is set to change that Watson has been restoring a 800 metre section of the waterway as part of the planning permission. The extensive work means the section of canal is set to be ‘in water’ by May 2027 The new section of waterway will also create a destination for visitors as a new café is planned alongside a canoe and kayaking school

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Longsight Manchester traders and residents living on city's worst road speak out as fears heighten Residents and traders have said the road is 'dangerous' but might not be able to be fixed. Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 06:06, 31 Aug 2026 Updated 06:54, 31 Aug 2026 Car horns are blaring on on Thursday afternoon A group of men are crossing the road but instead of using the designated crossing point, they wander out between the cars and make their way to the other side of shops, sparking fury among drivers There’s not a moment when traffic calms on this road over a couple of hours, and on the pavement there are at least 10 cars parked on double yellow lines One of the liveliest parts of the road is the junction with Slade Lane, where there are traffic lights filtering motorists. Two lanes each from from Slade Lane and Stockport Road merge, but because of the parked cars on Stockport Road, it effectively becomes four lanes merging in It has been dubbed Manchester’s ‘worst’ road. Many shopkeepers say they’ve seen accidents and deaths happen on a patch of tarmac which has been ‘horrendous’ since the 1990s

evidence_packet.summary: Cheshire Police Police officer who has shown 'no remorse over his actions' loses career William Matthews would have been sacked if he had not already resigned Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 06:41, 31 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Cheshire Constabulary ( A police officer sent and re
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cheshire Police Police officer who has shown 'no remorse over his actions' loses career William Matthews would have been sacked if he had not already resigned Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 06:41, 31 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Cheshire Constabulary ( A police officer sent and received messages on his mobile phone which 'indicated familiarity and association to controlled drug use and recreational use of Nitrous Oxide gas' Former police constable William Matthews would have been sacked had he not already resigned. A judgement arising from a misconduct hearing has now been published Former PC Matthews was working within a force's firearms department at the time. He was also said to have 'undertook online activity which indicated familiarity and association to controlled drug use and recreational use of Nitrous Oxide gas' The hearing at Cheshire Constabulary found the allegations to be proven. He resigned on August 3, ahead of the hearing Chief Constable Mark Roberts ruled former PC Matthews’ conduct was 'undoubtedly gross misconduct'

evidence_packet.title: Royal Manchester Children's Hospital's special message to Red Arrows after spectacular display
evidence_packet.lead: Royal Manchester Children's Hospital Royal Manchester Children's Hospital's special message to Red Arrows after spectacular display "Not only did you brighten up our grey Manchester sky, you certainly brightened up the day for many of our children" Co The world-famous aerobatics
evidence_packet.summary: Royal Manchester Children's Hospital Royal Manchester Children's Hospital's special message to Red Arrows after spectacular display "Not only did you brighten up our grey Manchester sky, you certainly brightened up the day for many of our children" Co The world-famous aerobatics
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Royal Manchester Children's Hospital Royal Manchester Children's Hospital's special message to Red Arrows after spectacular display "Not only did you brighten up our grey Manchester sky, you certainly brightened up the day for many of our children" Co The world-famous aerobatics display team of the RAF will be taking part in the Southport Airshow this weekend. On the return journey to RAF Warrington on Sunday, the team will fly directly over Greater Manchester, with a special flypast over the hospital The route saw the team fly over Lymm, onto Altrincham and then directly over the city centre, before heading out into Tameside and Oldham . From there, the team flew back to their base at RAF Waddington, in Lincolnshire Earlier this week, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust announced that the Red Arrows would be doing the flypast to 'support them and create a memorable moment' for the children receiving care at the Children's Hospital In a post, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust said: "We're excited to share that this bank holiday weekend we're in for a real treat - and we want you to enjoy it with us "The world-famous RAF Red Arrows will be carrying out a flypast over Royal Manchester Children's Hospital this Sunday at around 5.15pm - subject to weather and other operational factors on the day

Those living nearby fear plans to tackle that could make things worse. News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 17 People living near the A555 fear a plan to stop the road flooding could be a 'recipe for disaster' Less than 10 years old, the A555 has faced ‘longstanding challenges’, causing major disruption for drivers. The road links Stockport and Manchester Airport to the wider network but after it opened in 2018, it has been repeatedly affected by flooding Work was done to try and solve the problem but the road has still continued to flood. On New Year’s Eve and New Year's Day between 2024 and 2025, the road had to be completely closed to traffic Stockport council looked at what further measures could be taken with interventions to improve drainage around Woodford with work completed in July this year. Drainage from the Highfield Parkway housing estate and Woodford’s Recreation Ground will now be diverted into Spath Brook View 6 Images Flooding on the A555 in 2025 (Image: Jason Roberts /Manchester Evening News)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: NHS Northern Care Alliance in crisis: Failings, strikes and a backlog of complaints as NHS trust faces serious questions Fresh concerns over patient care at Northern Care Alliance, including a backlog of complaints and lengthy waits, have been laid ba News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 16:59, 30 Aug 2026 The Northern Care Alliance (NCA) has been warned that urgent action is needed to address patient care concerns - with the NHS trust facing a backlog of hundreds of complaints, according to newly published board The trust's own reports, published on Friday (August 28), show the NCA remains under pressure following a series of inspections and patient safety concerns The trust - which runs Salford Royal, Royal Oldham Hospital, Fairfield General Hospital and Rochdale Infirmary - has faced criticism after its own board papers revealed dozens of patients died or 'came to harm ' due to treatment delays and serious errors made by staff working und A total of 28 deaths were found to be linked to lengthy delays last year, with 56 issues of 'severe harm' and 10 deaths linked to problems diagnosing illness recorded The NCA has also faced disruption caused by strike action. Officers from Greater Manchester Police were called to reports of the serious incident at around 6pm on Saturday, August 19, at the restaurant on Riverside Walk A boy, aged 13, was taken to hospital with serious injuries. Two teenage boys have since been arrested on suspicion of assault and possession of a bladed article. Enquiries are ongoing, GMP say A man and his family, who were dining at the restaurant, witnessed the incident. evidence_packet.summary: Real Life ‘We lost our precious baby but became parents to three more beautiful children’ Tragedy was a 'signpost' to a new life for Sarah Hopes and her husband Tom Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 16:05, 30 Aug 2026 View 4 Images Sarah Hope Sarah Hopes and her husband
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Real Life ‘We lost our precious baby but became parents to three more beautiful children’ Tragedy was a 'signpost' to a new life for Sarah Hopes and her husband Tom Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 16:05, 30 Aug 2026 View 4 Images Sarah Hope Sarah Hopes and her husband Tom had always wanted their children close together in age. So when they found out they were pregnant again, when their daughter was just one, they were overjoyed However, just 12 weeks into the pregnancy, they received devastating news. Vet Sarah, 42, and IT manager Tom, 44, were informed that the baby had a serious fetal developmental abnormality known as Anencephaly, which affects the growth of the brain, skull, and scalp Medical staff told them the condition was 'incompatible with life' and recommended that they terminate the pregnancy Sarah said they had to have a ‘real conversation’ about what to do, but said: “We knew that our baby already had life and purpose inside the womb; he was ours and so wanted “There was a possibility he could live through a full-term pregnancy, and that we would meet him alive once born; we hoped and prayed this would be.”

evidence_packet.summary: Salford 'In the house Julius was killed, he got to his knees and begged for forgiveness' In December 2023, the body of Tanyaradzwa Julius Matera was found in undergrowth in Higher Broughton - now a coroner has demanded a new investigation into his mur News Neal Keeling Chief repo
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford 'In the house Julius was killed, he got to his knees and begged for forgiveness' In December 2023, the body of Tanyaradzwa Julius Matera was found in undergrowth in Higher Broughton - now a coroner has demanded a new investigation into his mur News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 15:52, 30 Aug 2026 Nearly two months after her friend Tanyaradzwa Julius Matera disappeared, Dorothy Wood attended a gathering at 99 Greater Cheetham Street West, Salford What she heard there would prompt a police search. That police search would spark a murder investigation Known as Julius by those closest to him, the 43-year-old was reported missing on October 24, 2023. By that time he had already been dead a week, and it would be 56 days before his body was found In that same Higher Broughton house, on the night of October 13 or early on October 14, police believe he was stabbed in the left side of his neck in a row over a bottle of cider The incident could have occurred in the communal kitchen, or a brick patio at its rear - just metres from where Dorothy would quiz Bennett Benjamin Nkonjera about Julius' disappearance at the gathering on December 2

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan 'They wouldn't let an animal suffer like this. It's my life, I should be able to choose what happens to it' Brian Griffin has incurable blood cancer. With the assisted dying bill - the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill - set to be debated News Iram Ramzan 07:00, 30 Aug 2026 Updated 07:19, 30 Aug 2026 Standing proud at almost 6ft at his home on a quiet cul-de-sac where he lives with wife Denise, it's hard to believe Brian Griffin is terminally ill. There's little to immediately suggest he is living on borrowed time For decades, Brian was a familiar figure at the front of the classroom, teaching biology and advanced skills to thousands of children across Wigan Among them were his own son and daughter, before he went on to lecture at the University of Manchester . Now the 74-year-old from Bryn is preparing to die, spending much of his remaining days considering how that will happen Brian invited the Manchester Evening News to his home to discuss the assisted dying bill - the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill - which will be debated in the Commons once again next month "If this Bill is passed, then in 30 years' time people will look back thinking 'they just used to let these people suffer - why?'," Brian says. "And I think people will just look back at it as absolutely barbaric."

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

evidence_packet.summary: The four school friends from Middleton, near Rochdale, have certainly come a long way since they hit the Manchester indie scene in 2006 While they have travelled around the world ever since, there is no place like home and they will take to the stage later for a huge homecoming g
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The four school friends from Middleton, near Rochdale, have certainly come a long way since they hit the Manchester indie scene in 2006 While they have travelled around the world ever since, there is no place like home and they will take to the stage later for a huge homecoming gig at Wythenshawe Park From humble beginnings performing for friends in the garden of their shared house in Burnage, the Courteeners are now celebrating 20 years together Fresh from releasing a new best-of compilation album called God Bless The Band, lead singer and songwriter Liam Fray spoke to BBC North West Tonight at The Briton's Protection pub on Deansgate, where he first performed as a solo artist back in 2005 Sitting upstairs in the pub, Fray smiled at the 3ft (0.9m) stage and single spotlight on the ceiling while recalling the night he spent there more than two decades ago "It's unusual to be in here and it's exactly the same," he said. "It is very small."

title: Manchester's adult services rated 'Good' by Care Quality Commission

evidence_packet.title: Manchester's adult services rated 'Good' by Care Quality Commission
evidence_packet.lead: A Care Quality Commission (CQC) inspection report published today (Wednesday 5 August) has found that Manchester City Council’s adult social care services are Good
evidence_packet.summary: A Care Quality Commission (CQC) inspection report published today (Wednesday 5 August) has found that Manchester City Council’s adult social care services are Good

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

It already has a strong tech base and devolution gives us a chance to align policy, funding and delivery more closely with what is happening on the ground To do that well, Combined Authorities and others need to understand that ecosystems are much broader and deeper than most public-facing institutions realise, that matters if they are going to make good decisions on skills, infrastructure, procurement and innovation support AI and emerging technologies clearly need focus because their impact will be felt across every part of the economy, but policy needs to keep pace with how those technologies are being used by businesses. Government and Combined Authorities will have more impact if they understand The new Digital Campus in Manchester is a good example of where this could become practical; a larger concentration of public sector digital capability in Manchester should create new routes for startups and scaleups to work with the government. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Imperial War Museum North (IWM North) , Manchester Until 31 August 2026 Additional information Always double check opening hours with the venue before making a special visit Spies, Lies and Deception comes to The Quays , cracking open a window into the shady world of espionage and secret operations that took place under the radar across the 20th and 21st centuries. The exhibition showcases how that carefully considered deception has shaped conflict. Hidden gadgets, forged documents and disguised weapons will show you the lengths spies would go to in order to conceal their work. Even the smallest of objects were considered. They would not rule out anything if they thought it might give them an edge against their enemy. A holl As well as cool gadgets that you should not attempt to make at home, there are personal stories which reveal true courage and tragic fate at the hands of espionage. You can learn about Noor Inayat Khan, the first female SOE wireless operator to be sent into Occupied France. As yo For the younger visitors, there is an interactive ‘Mission Room’ filled with coded clues and trails. Kids (and adults, there’s no age limit) can follow along and piece together the messages to be a part of their own spy missions Whether you are well versed in the history of war, deception and trickery, a long time fan of espionage, or a complete novice, this new exhibition at the Imperial War Museum North will have you questioning your own reality

evidence_packet.evidence_text: West Bromwich Albion have signed midfielder Toby Collyer from Manchester United for an undisclosed fee The 22-year-old, who has signed a four-year contract, spent the first half of last season at The Hawthorns, making 12 Championship appearances before moving to Hull City and helping them win promotion to the Premier League He is Albion's ninth summer signing so far, following new arrivals including Jimmy-Jay Morgan and Conor Townsend at the club Collyer made 13 appearances for Manchester United in all competitions during the 2024-25 season He made his competitive debut in their 3-0 home defeat by Liverpool in September 2024 "There were a few reasons why I was so keen to return," Collyer told Albion's website. , external

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC Four transfers Man United can complete before deadline as key position fixed and £36.5m man moves Manchester United are running out of time to get transfers done before deadline day Comments Sport opinion Jake Bayliss 04:30, 31 Aug 2026 View 3 Manchester United face an important end to the summer transfer window. The clock is ticking for Michael Carrick’s side to complete their business before Tuesday’s deadline United entered the summer intending to rebuild their midfield . The subsequent arrivals of Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba, combined with Kobbie Mainoo’s resurgence last season, mean there is now formidable competition for places However, other areas of the team could be strengthened ahead of a gruelling campaign, as United look to compete across multiple competitions. Для многих украинцев за границей ее концерт станет не только художественным Наталья Карпа получила два высших образования, однако именно музыка стала делом ее жизни. От первых фестивалей и конкурсов до больших сцен Украины и мира, от песни “Калина”, открывшей ей путь к широкому признанию, до многочисленных сольных концертов и международных туров для укра Заслуженная артистка Украины, автор десятков популярных композиций, продюсер и общественный деятель в своем репертуаре легко сочетает лирическую нежность и праздничную энергию, а рядом с хорошо известными хитами непременно звучат новые композиции. Недаром поклонники после концерт В Лондоне прозвучат песни, сопровождавшие разные поколения украинцев, будут звучать слова, в которых живут любовь, вера и несокрушимость. Музыка преодолевает расстояния, находит дорогу к сердцу независимо от того, где человек живет сегодня, и оставляет после себя огонь жизни! evidence_packet.evidence_text: Events EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters Official Chamber Post FREE Online Thursday 10 Sep 10am - 11am Book Now About the event The way low-value goods enter the European Union is changing From 1 July 2026, the EU introduced a new €3 customs duty on low-value consignments valued up to €150 entering the EU from outside the bloc. The change removes the previous duty exemption and introduces new considerations for businesses exporting goods directly to EU customers The new duty applies based on product categories/tariff classifications rather than simply per parcel, meaning shipments containing different types of goods could face multiple charges. For example, a parcel containing products under different tariff headings may attract multiple While the change is aimed largely at addressing the growth of low-value e-commerce imports, it will also impact UK businesses selling products directly into EU markets, including online retailers, brands and SMEs What the new €3 EU customs duty means for UK businesses
